text.p: American Business Information Inc said Tuesday it is restating its financial statements for the first quarter of calendar 1997 and for the 1995 fourth quarter and year-end.
For the first quarter of calendar 1997, the company said it will be reducing its effect on earnings resulting from the Database America acquisition by $18 million.

The previously reported first quarter results had been based on estimates available at the time the first quarter results were released, and ABI has now completed its valuation of the tangible and intangible assets acquired in the acquisition.

As a result of the restatement, the revised first quarter charge resulting from the Database America acquisition will be $52 million, and the company's reported loss for the first quarter will be reduced to $47.4 million, or $2.04 per share, instead of the previously reported loss of $65.4 million, or $2.82 per share.

About $12 million of the reduction will be amortized over the last three quarters of 1997, with the remainder amortized principally over the 15 year life previously assigned to goodwill in the transaction, it said.

The 1995 restatement will result in an after-tax charge to 1995 earnings of about $2.4 million, principally the result of a previously reported acquisition by the company of 291,875 shares from a former ABI officer.

The company said that it has determined based on advice of its outside auditors, that a compensation charge should be taken because it repurchased the shares within six months of the former officer's acquisition of such shares.
As a result of the restatement, ABI's 1995 profit will be $11.9 million, or $0.58 per share, instead of previously reported $14.3 million, or $0.69 per share.
ABI compiles information on businesses and consumers in the United States and Canada and provides data processing and analytical services.
